newsitem.title: LEBANON: Katyusha rockets from S.Lebanon hit Israel border.
newsitem.headline: Katyusha rockets from S.Lebanon hit Israel border.

text.p: Suspected pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas fired more than 30 Katyusha rockets towards Israel late on Wednesday, a pro-Israeli militia source said.
"A number of Katyusha rockets were fired from outside the Israel occupation zone and landed at the Israeli border. Some may have hit northern Israel," said the source.
"More than 30 rockets were fired towards Israel," he added.
Residents said they saw more than 30 Katyusha rockets fired towards the security zone Israel occupies inside south Lebanon.
There were no immediate reports of casualties and Hizbollah was not immediately available for confirmation of the rocket attacks.
Residents said some rockets had landed near the Israeli outpost of Blat inside the zone.
The rockets were fired one day after Hizbollah (Party of God) threatened to carry out suicide bombings inside Israel and Arab land occupied by the Jewish state.
A Hizbollah leader last month threatened further rocket assaults on northern Israel if Lebanese civilians fell victim again to Israeli attacks.
The latest rocket attacks on Israeli forces and their local militia allies in the zone come at a time of high Middle East tensions.

Crown Prince Hassan of Jordan failed in talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jerusalem on Wednesday to persuade Israel to end sanctions it imposed on Palestinians after a double suicide bombing.

Hizbollah is fighting to drive some 1,000 Israel troops and their local militia allies from the 15-km (nine-mile) occupation zone which is the site of frequent rocket attacks, clashes and roadside bombs.

Israel and Hizbollah undertook not to fire on civilian targets as part of a 1996 ceasefire that ended a 17-day Israeli onslaught in which about 200 people -- mainly Lebanese civilians -- were killed. Hizbollah also undertook not to launch attacks from within Lebanese villages.
